common_name: Nearctic Woodland Obscura Fly (Distal Tarsomere Sex Comb)

scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila affinis (2.4 µm, detail scale)

predecessor.note: Project chronoseries predecessor. Amber inclusion; the published sibling slot is a cellular tergite wavelength, not this detail tier.

successor.note: Project chronoseries successor (virilis group). Not an ancestor-descendant claim. Puparial pigment scale, not the obscura-group granule wave.

evolutionary_history.what_changes: At 0 Ma and 2.444 µm the same Turing wavenumber law is evaluated 40.3× finer than berryi's 98.43 µm cellular assignment (19 Ma) and 56.8× finer than americana's 138.7 µm primordium assignment (0 Ma). Diffusivity ratio Dv/Du = 10 and Du are solved for λ_c = 2.444 µm; they are not the sibling slots' alpha_scale power-law coefficients. The selected form is a spot field inside a 48.88 µm × 36.66 µm ocellar/tergite patch (300 classical wavelengths), not a body-scale stripe.

equations.activator: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + Du laplacian(u)
equations.inhibitor: dv/dt = b - u^2 v + Dv laplacian(v)
equations.stability_without_diffusion: trace(J) = f_u + g_v < 0 and det(J) = u0^2 > 0
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (Dv f_u + Du g_v) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.turing_condition: (Dv f_u + Du g_v) > 0 and (Dv f_u + Du g_v)^2 > 4 Du Dv det(J)
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic on a rectangular patch; no-flux is not used

parameters.note: Du and Dv are derived in the script from k_c so that lambda_c = 2.444 µm at ratio 10. They are not stored as a copied sibling alpha_scale.

empirical_claims: Turing 1952: a homogeneous chemical steady state that is stable without diffusion can be unstable at a finite wavenumber k_c when the inhibitor diffuses sufficiently faster than the activator.
Schnakenberg 1979: the two-species mass-action system a - u + u^2 v, b - u^2 v has a unique positive steady state and can oscillate or, with diffusion, form patterns.

Sturtevant 1916 described Drosophila affinis from North America. Miller 1955 compared sex combs of D. affinis and D. athabasca; the distal-tarsomere comb is the species diagnosis, not the 2.444 µm wavelength.

Wittkopp, True and Carroll 2002: Yellow and Ebony jointly place melanin in the adult cuticle. Wittkopp, Carroll and Kopp 2003 review the genetic control of Drosophila pigment patterns at the tergite scale, which is coarser than this detail tier.

Shoup 1966 described ommatidial pigment-granule ontogeny in D. melanogaster. Transfer of that cellular mechanism to D. affinis granule spacing is a transfer boundary; this loop does not report a new electron-microscope measurement.

The vendored habitus photograph carries a 250 µm scale bar. A 2.444 µm wavelength is not resolved in that image. Image comparison therefore scores the adult habitus, while the wavelength law is scored against the dispersion relation.
